deep.reconstruction:
Setting: put θ = ∛n and α = x + yθ + zθ² in Z[θ]. The cubic form on the page is the norm N(α) = x³ + n y³ + n² z³ − 3n x y z. This is the determinant of multiplication by α on the basis 1, θ, θ².

Claim on the page: if A (or a multiple kA) is represented by this form, then n is a cubic residue mod A. A cube root of n mod A is given by any of three equal fractions:
∛n ≡ (x²−nyz)/(nz²−xy) ≡ (ny²−nxz)/(x²−nyz) ≡ (nz²−xy)/(y²−xz) (mod A).

Reconstruction of the reasoning (implicit steps mine, but certain):

(1) Adjugate element. Put
- a = x² − nyz,
- b = nz² − xy,
- c = y² − xz,
- α' = a + bθ + cθ².
Direct multiplication gives α·α' = N. The θ- and θ²-coefficients cancel identically. So α' is the product of the two conjugates of α, i.e. the adjugate.

(2) Key identities (mine). Computed identically in Z[x,y,z,n]:
- a² − nbc = x·N,
- b² − ac = z·N,
- nc² − ab = y·N.
These say the adjugate matrix of the multiplication matrix has rank ≤ 1 whenever det = N vanishes.

(3) Hence if A | N:
- a² ≡ nbc, b² ≡ ac, nc² ≡ ab (mod A).
- So a/b ≡ nc/a (equivalent to a² ≡ nbc), and a/b ≡ b/c (equivalent to b² ≡ ac), provided the denominators are invertible mod A. These are exactly Gauss's three fractions: (x²−nyz)/(nz²−xy) = a/b, (ny²−nxz)/(x²−nyz) = nc/a, (nz²−xy)/(y²−xz) = b/c.
- Put t = a/b. Then a³ = a·a² ≡ nabc and b³ = b·b² ≡ abc, so t³ ≡ n.
- Identically, a³ − n b³ = N·(ax − nbz).
- So n is a cubic residue mod A and t is a cube root, i.e. (a, b, c) ≡ c·(t², t, 1).

Purpose: this is the cubic analogue of 'p | x² + ny² ⇒ −n is a quadratic residue mod p, with √(−n) ≡ x/y'. It gives a criterion and an explicit cube root for cubic residuacity via the norm form of the pure cubic ring Z[∛n]. It belongs to Gauss's investigations of cubic residues and cubic forms.
errors: Not an error in the algebra, but an unstated hypothesis: the fractions require the denominators (nz²−xy, x²−nyz, y²−xz) to be invertible mod A. For composite A, or when x, y, z share factors with A (e.g. α ≡ 0 mod a prime of A, making a ≡ b ≡ c ≡ 0), the statement as written can fail or become vacuous. Some coprimality condition (e.g. gcd(b, A) = 1, or gcd(A, n) = 1 and the representation primitive) is tacitly assumed.
The three expressions are equal mod A only via the identities a² − nbc = xN, b² − ac = zN, nc² − ab = yN. Gauss states the equalities without proof; they are correct.

results.what: x³ + ny³ + n²z³ − 3nxyz is the norm of x + y∛n + z∛n², with adjugate (x²−nyz) + (nz²−xy)∛n + (y²−xz)∛n²
results.modern_name: Norm form of the pure cubic order Z[∛n]; circulant-type determinant
results.usually_credited_to: Euler and Lagrange (Lagrange's Additions to Euler's Algebra, 1770s, on multiplicative cubic forms)

results.what: If A divides x³ + ny³ + n²z³ − 3nxyz (with suitable coprimality), then n is a cubic residue mod A and ∛n ≡ (x²−nyz)/(nz²−xy) ≡ n(y²−xz)/(x²−nyz) ≡ (nz²−xy)/(y²−xz)
results.modern_name: Primes dividing a norm from Q(∛n) split, giving a root of t³ − n mod p (Dedekind–Kummer style); explicit root from the rank-1 adjugate
results.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Euler/Lagrange/Gauss work on cubic residues; general theory Dedekind (1870s–1880s)

deep.surprise_reason: An elementary, correct observation, the direct cubic analogue of the familiar quadratic fact. It fits Gauss's known (partly published in Werke) work on cubic residues and cubic forms. The explicit cube-root formula is a nice detail but not a significant result unknown to the literature.

a² − nbc = xN, so a/b ≡ nc/a mod A when A | N (result 0)
b² − ac = zN, so a/b ≡ b/c mod A when A | N (result 0)
